macro.headline: Hawkish Fed, energy & geopolitics in the driver's seat
macro.body: Fed Chair Warsh scrapped forward guidance and the dot plot leans toward hikes, not cuts, so long-duration high-multiple growth (NOW, ADBE, NVDA, IOT) stays rate-sensitive. Energy and the Strait of Hormuz headlines are the live swing factor on inflation.

risk.detail: FY guide cut (Jun 4): Americas comps −5% (5th straight), tariffs gutted margins, China stalled.
FY26 growth cut 10.5→7–8.5%; Watchman/EP/urology soft; mgmt guides flat through Q3.
Beat & raised (Jun 11) yet sold off; AI-moat fear (Claude Design), CFO exit, ARR de-emphasis — the narrative, not the numbers, drives it.
China export-license tightening + Senate scrutiny; the memory/chip complex swings on AI-spending sentiment.
No bad news — strong Q1, IBM AI deal. But it's the biggest weight + a high multiple; in a hawkish-Fed software de-rate it leads the drawdown.
Trump MFN pricing deals (Gilead, Novartis signed) + import tariffs put a pricing-pressure overhang on the whole pharma cluster.
FY EPS guide cut on deal financing + a weak flu season; revenue raised. Defensive — a yellow flag, not a red one.

sectors.driver: The industry pulls back from earlier gains
sectors.note: As the industry pulls back from earlier gains, possibly due to pressure from Asia as ChangXin Memory Technologies prepares for its Shanghai STAR Market debut. Industry weakness could result from investors adopting a risk-off stance amid a broader AI-related pullback.

sectors.driver: Recent earnings from ServiceNow and SAP help assuage concerns over AI en…
sectors.note: As recent earnings from ServiceNow and SAP help assuage concerns over AI encroachment. Also, recent investor unease over AI-related capex spending by hyperscalers and steep valuations for semiconductor-related companies may be bolstering confidence in the software sector.

sectors.driver: Surging oil prices and Treasury yields weigh on sentiment
sectors.note: As surging oil prices and Treasury yields weigh on sentiment, with the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield climbing to its highest level since January 2025. Rising yields and energy prices have fueled inflation concerns, reinforcing expectations that interest rates will remain elevated and raising concerns about slower loan demand and economic growth.
